scope: Portable verification candidate; installer and Mac builds deferred until user verification.

bossWorkspace.launch: Final production archive loaded under a metadata-matched Electron launcher.
tests: Production Windows shell creates three sandboxed isolated native chat views and keeps its browser session in memory.
Import and Normal OK open exactly three distinct chats with the boss coordinator active.
A mixed text, valid PDF and PNG source selection reaches all three native file inputs; Reset clears the staged previews and retains the session.
One native file picker uploads the original source to the boss and both workers.
The boss writes distinct worker instructions, receives both results and exact generated files every cycle, then both workers verify one final candidate after four improvement cycles.
The real boss composer accepts an instruction during worker generation, delivers it in the next boss context, and completes the run with no queued message left behind.
Native Save downloads the actual accepted file and matches the coordinator SHA-256, with the requested corrected values.
The settings selector applies Horror, Alien, Night, Cyberpunk and Anime backgrounds to all three real chat views.
Robot, Explorer and Spirit character choices apply without changing the active chat run or its accepted files.
Clicking the center boss opens and closes its sliding native chat panel while preserving the worker workspace.
A follow-up reuses all three conversations; a new instruction while the boss generates is queued safely.
Stop cancels active boss generation and prevents queued instructions from restarting the stopped run.
Stop also cancels both workers during their concurrent generation, retaining each completed conversation.
Accelerated localhost-only supervision checks both real active worker bridges repeatedly without stopping or resending their healthy generation. Production keeps its five-minute interval.
A genuine stopped-thinking header without an answer is recovered only for its exact owned worker; the boss waits for the healthy peer and bottom monitoring shows both observations.
The recovery boss receives only actual completed peer evidence plus the interruption report, creates fresh useful worker prompts and does not count the abandoned pair as a work cycle.

After genuine interruption recovery, both workers independently accept one exact final candidate; its actual boss answer, bottom answer, remaining limitation and exported monitoring report all match the completed run.
Reset clears all three chats without clearing the imported session; Work mode is verified on the fresh boss and worker pages.
Temporary mode is also verified on all three new chats through its visible page controls.
Unreadable boss control output receives one format repair, then stops safely without dispatching an invented worker task or clearing the session.
Production shell opens three sandboxed pages using only isolated offline fixture data.
One sidebar click reads a 100 MB PDF through the native picker and confirms delivery to the whole team.
All three real Chromium file inputs independently hash the exact 100 MB source bytes and receive it once.
Actual Electron page-request IPC uses sequential 1 MB chunks and one commit per page.
The sidebar returns to ready state and all three page bridges remain responsive after upload.
The completed large-file workspace closes and disposes its three owned browser pages cleanly.

nativePortableStartup.providerScope: Empty isolated session; no authentication, provider navigation or live model task
nativePortableStartup.clipboardScope: The Windows startup smoke does not access the clipboard

verificationLimits: Provider responses and upload previews used controlled offline fixtures; no live ChatGPT task or account limit was tested for 1.8.2.
Long response scheduling used controlled clocks; this is not evidence of a real one-hour remote analysis.
The 100 MiB check establishes exact app-to-file-input upload transport, not remote service acceptance or large generated-file downloads.
Agreement between models is not proof of correctness or external test execution.
